response_text: In this lab we assumed the stack is structured with the MSP at the “top” of the stack, taking up some amount of memory, and each of the process stacks (thread stacks) are sequentially below the main stack. Each of the process stacks take up the same amount of memory, which may or may not be the same as the main stack. In this lab we assume that both the main and process stacks take up 0x400 bytes, or 1024 bytes, in memory. As the stack is stored sequentially like an array, by knowing the MSP_init_val, we can add the size of the main stack (0x400) to its start point in memory (MSP_init_val) to find its endpoint, which is also the start point of the first process stack, which is PSP_val.\n
